title: Microsoft Purview: auto-archiving for Exchange Online mailboxes (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: Hold: the E5 archive-capacity statement omits Microsoft's instruction to keep Records Management enabled in the user's licence settings. The documented controls and roadmap facts check out, including the explicitly reported differences over the threshold and organisation-wide disabling.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn's threshold section and archive-mailboxes page say 100 disables auto-archiving, while its considerations say it cannot be disabled at organisation level.
claims.quote: Auto-archiving can't be disabled at the organization level, however autoarchive threshold can be configured for organization. ... Setting the threshold to **100 disables auto-archiving for the tenant**.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Managed Folder Assistant monitors mailbox size and performs the move automatically without a separate approval step.
claims.quote: The Managed Folder Assistant continuously monitors the primary mailbox size. ... Managed Folder Assistant automatically archives the **oldest** items first until usage drops below the threshold.

claims.claim: Auto-archiving works towards bringing mailbox usage below the threshold and does not trigger for usage below it.
claims.quote: When mailbox utilization exceeds 96% of its quota, items are automatically moved to the archive mailbox until usage drops below the threshold.

claims.claim: Each run attempts to move 3% of the applicable quota.
claims.quote: Auto-Archiving attempts to move 3% of data in each run until mailbox size is below the threshold. Percentage is calculated based on ProhibitSendReceiveQuota/RecoverableItemsQuota.

claims.claim: Data received less than 60 days ago is not archived.
claims.quote: Auto-Archiving doesn't archive data received less than 60 days ago.

claims.claim: The same threshold-based approach applies to Recoverable Items folders approaching their quota.
claims.quote: The same concept applies to Recoverable Items ("Dumpster") folders when they near their quota.

claims.claim: Threshold-based auto-archiving complements existing time-based archiving policies.
claims.quote: Auto-archiving introduces threshold-based archiving that complements existing time-based archiving policies.

claims.claim: Auto-archiving does not change deletion policies or behaviour.
claims.quote: No, auto-archiving relocates items to the archive to prevent primary mailbox quota lockouts but doesn't change deletion or retention behaviors.

claims.claim: Auto-archiving does not change retention policies or behaviour.
claims.quote: The feature doesn't change deletion or retention policies.

claims.quote: Does auto-archiving enable auto-expanding archives? No, auto-expanding archives must be enabled manually to ensure no disruptions when the main archive is full.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The auto-archiving page publishes no separate price for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: '"auto-archiving" "price" "meter" Exchange Online'; opened auto-archiving, archive-mailboxes and the Purview service description's email-archiving licensing section. The feature page's Pricing section names existing archiving licences, not a separate price.

claims.claim: The auto-archiving page publishes no separate meter for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: '"auto-archiving" "price" "meter" Exchange Online'; opened auto-archiving, archive-mailboxes and the Purview service description's email-archiving licensing section. No auto-archiving meter is stated; returned SharePoint meters concern different services.

claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoArchivingThresholdPercentage 90 sets the tenant-wide auto-archiving threshold using Exchange PowerShell.
claims.quote: Module: Exchange PowerShell ... -AutoArchivingThresholdPercentage ... Applicable: Exchange Online ... Type: Int16

claims.claim: An admin-centre UI for the auto-archiving threshold is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Exchange Online auto-archiving AutoArchivingThresholdPercentage AutoArchivingEnabled admin center UI diagnostics'; opened auto-archiving and Set-OrganizationConfig. The documented threshold control is PowerShell; no matching admin-centre route was returned.

claims.claim: Set-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoArchivingEnabled $false disables auto-archiving for that mailbox using Exchange PowerShell.
claims.quote: Module: Exchange PowerShell ... -AutoArchivingEnabled ... Applicable: Exchange Online ... Type: Boolean ... The Identity parameter specifies the mailbox that you want to modify.

claims.claim: An admin-centre UI for the per-mailbox auto-archiving switch is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Exchange Online auto-archiving AutoArchivingThresholdPercentage AutoArchivingEnabled admin center UI diagnostics'; opened auto-archiving and Set-Mailbox. Only the PowerShell enable/disable setting was documented; Outlook AutoArchive is a different feature.

claims.claim: The archive switch is at Exchange admin center > Recipients > Mailboxes > mailbox > Others > Mailbox archive > Manage mailbox archive > Mailbox archive.
claims.quote: navigate to **Recipients** > **Mailboxes**. ... select the user ... select **Others**, and under **Mailbox archive**, select **Manage mailbox archive** ... turn on **Mailbox archive**

claims.claim: Enable-Mailbox -Identity <username> -Archive enables an archive mailbox using Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Run the following command to enable the archive mailbox for a single user.
Enable-Mailbox -Identity <username> -Archive

claims.claim: Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive enables auto-expanding archiving for a user with a cloud-based primary mailbox.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving for a specific user, run the following command. ... Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.claim: No admin-centre UI is documented for enabling auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: Searched: '"auto-expanding archiving" "Exchange admin center" enable'; opened enable-autoexpanding-archiving, which states: 'You can't use the Exchange admin center or the Microsoft Purview portal to enable auto-expanding archiving.'

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving cannot be turned off once enabled.
claims.quote: After you turn on auto-expanding archiving for your organization or for a specific user, it can't be turned off.

claims.claim: The archive mailbox must already be enabled before enabling auto-expanding archiving for that user.
claims.quote: A user's mailbox must already be enabled for archive before you can enable auto-expanding archiving.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving adds archive storage, providing a separate way to address archive-capacity pressure.
claims.quote: When auto-expanding archiving is turned on, additional storage space is automatically added to a user's archive mailbox until it reaches the storage limit of 1.5 TB.

claims.claim: Export-MailboxDiagnosticLogs -Identity <user mailbox> -ComponentName MRM retrieves auto-archiving diagnostics using the Exchange Online shell.
claims.quote:
Administrators can access detailed diagnostics using the Exchange Online shell for individual mailbox:
Export-MailboxDiagnosticLogs -Identity <user mailbox> -ComponentName MRM

claims.claim: No admin-centre UI is documented for diagnostics showing what auto-archiving moved and its trigger.
claims.quote: Searched: '"auto-archiving" "admin center" threshold mailbox diagnostics permissions consent identity'; opened auto-archiving and enable-archive-mailboxes. Archive-mailbox troubleshooting tests are documented, but no UI for the feature's movement log and trigger was found.

claims.claim: The diagnostics are read-only and report archived items and the triggering threshold.
claims.quote: Items archived till date: <Date>. Total items archived: <ItemCount>, Total bytes archived: <Size>. Auto-Archiving was triggered to move <xyz GB> of data because mailbox utilization crossed 96%.

claims.claim: The documented automation for these controls is Exchange Online PowerShell, with no other automation surface documented for auto-archiving.
claims.quote: Searched: '"AutoArchivingEnabled" "Graph" "REST"'; opened auto-archiving, archive enablement, auto-expanding enablement, Set-Mailbox and Set-OrganizationConfig. The returned Graph mail overview does not document an auto-archiving setting; the controls use Exchange PowerShell.

claims.claim: Learn gives no named role for the auto-archiving threshold cmdlet.
claims.quote: Searched: '"AutoArchivingThresholdPercentage" "role" permissions'; opened auto-archiving and Set-OrganizationConfig. The reference says permissions are required and links to cmdlet-permission discovery, but names no role for this threshold parameter.
